annual.label: Annual report fee
annual.due: By September 30 each year, starting the year after the LLC is formed.

Pennsylvania Department of State - Fees and payments

amount.note: Fee for LLCs and other for-profit entities. LLCs with a not-for-profit purpose pay nothing. The first report is due the year after formation.

notIncluded.label: Reinstatement after dissolution
notIncluded.reason: Only if the LLC is dissolved for not filing annual reports. The Department lists a reinstatement fee plus a fee for each missing report.

sources.title: Pennsylvania Department of State - Annual reports

notIncluded.label: Registered agent service
notIncluded.reason: Only if you hire a registered agent. The agent sets the price, so it is not a state fee and is not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Name reservation
notIncluded.reason: Optional. Reserving a name before you file is a separate charge and is not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Expedited filing and certified copies
notIncluded.reason: Optional. Faster processing and certified copies cost extra and are not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Local business licenses and permits
notIncluded.reason: City, county and industry licenses depend on where the business operates and what it does. None are in the total.

notIncluded.label: Federal and state income taxes
notIncluded.reason: Taxes on the LLC's or its owners' income are not part of this estimate. This page is not legal or tax advice.

content.intro: {state} charges a one-time fee to file a Certificate of Organization and a small annual report fee each year after that.

howItWorks.text: The Department of State lists the fee for a domestic LLC's Certificate of Organization and the annual report fee for for-profit entities.
LLCs file the annual report by the end of September. The first report is due the year after formation.
An LLC that does not file can be administratively dissolved and loses the exclusive right to its name.

faq.q: What happens if a {state} LLC skips the annual report?
faq.text: The Department says it can be administratively dissolved and lose the exclusive right to its name. Reinstatement costs extra.
